text:
JJ Peterka is in his first season in Boston after a year in Utah, and the Bruins are getting about what the numbers promised: 6 goals and 15 points in 23 games on a little over 17 minutes a night, with the Bruins winning seven of his last ten.

"Every time JJ Peterka shoots, you're reminded why he should shoot more," 98.5 The Sports Hub's Ty Anderson posted after his goal in Detroit. Fair point. He has 47 shots, a quiet stretch of three shotless games in his last eight, and 7.5 expected goals against six actual. Nothing here is lucky: his shooting (12.8%) sits right in his likely range, and the points per 60 match the 2.15 we think he is.

At 5v5 Boston takes 53% of the expected goals with him on, about level with the team overall. Evolving-Hockey said he was better than his goals last season too (1.5 expected wins against zero actual), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck. If the shot volume climbs, the scoring will follow it.
